newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb Cty, Ga., okays school, property tax plans.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb Cty, Ga., okays school, property tax plans.

text.p: Voters in Georgia's DeKalb County approved a one-cent sales tax increase for schools and another one-cent sales tax increase to offset property tax rollbacks, elections officials said Wednesday.
The DeKalb County school district was one of 69 Georgia school districts voting Tuesday on the local option tax for schools.
A constitutional amendment approved by voters in November allowed districts to levy the one-cent tax increase for up to five years to fund school construction and retire outstanding debt.
DeKalb votes approved the school tax by a 2-1 margin, with 47,388 yes votes and 21,855 no votes.
Separately, DeKalb voters approved a proposal to raise sales taxes to offset reductions in property taxes. That proposal passed with 70 percent of the votes, or 49,592 yes votes and 21,650 no votes.

In January, the General Assembly gave the county permission to levy the homestaed option sales tax if approved by voters. The law is expected to be expanded to apply to six other counties that do not have local-option or special use sales taxes.
Together, the referendums will raise DeKalb's sales tax to seven percent from five percent, and virtually eliminate non-school-related property taxes.
